reports.title: Agilent Reports Fourth-Quarter Fiscal Year 2026 Financial Results

lines: •Excluding the net benefit of tariff refunds recognized in fiscal year 2026, non-GAAP fiscal year 2027 operating margin expansion(2) at the midpoint of core revenue guidance is expected to be approximately 70 basis points higher relative to 26.8% in fiscal year 2026.
Excluding the net benefit of tariff refunds recognized in fiscal year 2026, EPS growth is expected to be 8.5% to 10.5%.

desk.headline: Revenue up 9.6% to $2.04bn and adjusted EPS of $1.86, both above estimates; FY27 outlook initiated above consensus

other.label: Adjusted operating margin
other.change: +2.8 pts y/y, incl. ~1.2 pts tariff refunds

results: Q4 revenue rose 9.6% to $2.04bn (8.3% core), above the $1.99bn estimate; adjusted EPS of $1.86 beat the $1.73 estimate.
Tariff refunds helped: they added $0.07 to adjusted EPS and about 1.2 points to the 30.0% adjusted operating margin.
All three groups grew: Applied Markets +13%, Life Sciences and Diagnostics +12% (+9% core) and CrossLab +6%, with margins up in each.
Full year: revenue $7.55bn (+8.7%), adjusted EPS $6.34 (+13%) and GAAP EPS $5.15 (+13%).
FY26 operating cash flow was $1.65bn; Agilent spent $951m on acquisitions, $323m on buybacks and $288m on dividends.

guidance.summary: First outlook for FY27: revenue of $8.00–8.15bn (5–7% core growth) and adjusted EPS of $6.73–6.86, both a little above consensus. It excludes any further tariff refunds.

points: CEO Padraig McDonnell said growth built each quarter, crediting sales execution and the Ignite cost and operating programme.
China revenue rose 19%, with pharma there up more than 40%; the FY27 plan assumes only mid-single-digit China growth.
Instrument sales grew at a mid-teens rate, and management said the lab equipment replacement cycle is less than half done.
Pharma reshoring brought tens of millions in orders in FY26, seen as a roughly $300m opportunity over three to four years.
Management said FY27 revenue could reach the top of the range if momentum holds, with growth stronger in the first half.
call.source: Call coverage: MarketBeat via Yahoo Finance, 23 Nov 2026; TipRanks, 24 Nov 2026

watch: Whether growth holds up without tariff-refund help as comparisons get harder in the second half.
China and pharma demand against the cautious mid-single-digit China assumption.
Start-up costs of the new Train C capacity, flagged as a margin headwind.
